claims.text: What the image looks like Periph colon > 6 cm w haustra; cecum > 9 cm → lrg bowel obstruct
claims.quote: Peripheral colon >6 cm with haustra; cecum >9 cm Large bowel obstruction

claims.text: Radiograph: distention of the colon prox to the obstruct
claims.quote: In large-bowel obstruction, abdominal radiograph shows distention of the colon proximal to the obstruction.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Lrg bowel: periph “picture frame”; haustra do ⍉cross the full diameter; dilated > 6 cm (> 9 cm @ the cecum)
claims.quote: Large bowel = peripheral 'picture frame', haustra do NOT cross full diameter, dilated >6 cm (>9 cm at cecum).

claims.text: Perf can occur w marked dilate; the risk = ↑if the cecum = ≥ 13 cm
claims.quote: Perforation may occur in an ischemic segment (typically small bowel) or when marked dilation occurs. The risk is high if the cecum is dilated to a diameter ≥ 13 cm.

claims.text: Eti Colon: tumors (USU Lt colon), diverticulitis (USU sigmoid), volvulus of the sigmoid or cecum, fecal impaction, Hirschsprung dz, Crohn dz
claims.quote: Colon | Tumors (usually in left colon), diverticulitis (usually in sigmoid), volvulus of sigmoid or cecum, fecal impaction, Hirschsprung disease, Crohn disease

claims.text: Strangulation = rare in large-bowel obstruct (except w volvulus)
claims.quote: In large-bowel obstruction, strangulation is rare (except with volvulus).

claims.text: Sx USU milder and more gradual than SBO: increasing constipation → obstipation and distention; vomiting may occur (USU several hrs later) but = ⍉common; lower abd cramps w.o passing stool
claims.quote: Obstruction of the large bowel usually causes milder symptoms that develop more gradually than those caused by small-bowel obstruction. Increasing constipation leads to obstipation and abdominal distention. Vomiting may occur (usually several hours after onset of other symptoms) but is not common. Lower abdominal cramps unproductive of feces occur.

claims.text: Exam typically: distended abd w loud borborygmi, ⍉tenderness, rectum USU empty; a mass @ an obstructing tumor may be palpable
claims.quote: Physical examination typically shows a distended abdomen with loud borborygmi. There is no tenderness, and the rectum is usually empty. A mass corresponding to the site of an obstructing tumor may be palpable.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: CT; surg consult
Supportive care as for SBO: nasogastric suction, IVF and a urinary cath to monitor output
claims.quote: Supportive care is similar for small- and large-bowel obstruction: nasogastric suction, IV fluids (0.9% saline or lactated Ringer’s solution for intravascular volume repletion), and a urinary catheter to monitor fluid output.

claims.text: Obstructing colon CA: sometimes a single-stage resection and anastomosis (± a temp colostomy or ileostomy); otherwise a diverting colostomy w delayed resection
claims.quote: Obstructing colon cancers can sometimes be treated by a single-stage resection and anastomosis, with or without a temporary colostomy or ileostomy. When this procedure is not possible, a diverting colostomy with delayed resection is recommended.

claims.text: Obstruct from diverticulitis: perf = often present; removal = indicated w perf and gen peritonitis — resection and colostomy, w anastomosis often postponed
claims.quote: When diverticulitis causes obstruction, perforation is often present. Removal of the involved area may be very difficult but is indicated if perforation and general peritonitis are present. Resection and colostomy are done, and anastomosis is often postponed.
